reasoning you have not seen. The change is already applied in this worktree. You can read the
repository, and you can run tests through `aih check`, the only command available:
`aih check <test files...>` runs those tests, `--race` under the race detector and
`--run <pattern>` only matching tests (when the project supports them), and
`aih check --probe <file>` runs a scratch test you wrote as a NEW file named `aih_probe*` and
deletes it afterwards. You cannot edit the change: every other file is locked for you. The harness
has already verified mechanically that the diff stays within the task's files, that the changed
tests fail without the production change and pass with it, and that the whole suite is green. Do
not re-check those. Your job is judgement, backed by tests you run.

## Original request

Harden upgraded-stream handling in `reverse_proxy` across config reloads (caddyserver/caddy
PR #7649 scope).

Long-lived upgraded connections through the reverse proxy (WebSocket and other `Upgrade`
tunnels, HTTP/2 extended CONNECT) keep the whole handler and config alive across reloads, so a
server that reloads often holds on to old configs, and the current behaviour on reload (close every
upgraded stream, optionally after a delay) is the only option. Middleware and response writers also
misbehave once a connection has been hijacked, and operators cannot see what their streams are
doing.

Required behaviour:

- A new opt-in `reverse_proxy` setting, `stream_detached`: when set, upgraded streams are detached
  from the config lifecycle and survive a reload; on reload only the streams whose upstream was
  removed from the new config are closed. The default stays as today: upgraded streams are closed on
  reload, honouring the existing close-delay behaviour.
- A `stream_logs` block with a `skip_handshake` option to suppress access logging of the upgrade
  handshake (default: logged), with stream close logs available in the access log via
  `logger_name access`, and a configurable log level (default DEBUG).
- Upgraded streams must keep working through the other handlers of a route: `encode`, `intercept`
  with `handle_response`, access logging. Once a connection is hijacked, nothing may write to the
  response again; a 101 is the final response for an upgrade; the proxy copies bytes on the raw
  connection, not through the recording response writer.
- HTTP/2 extended CONNECT (RFC 8441) upgrades keep working, as do HTTP/1.1 upgrades in detached
  mode.
- Stream observability metrics in `reverse_proxy`: active streams, streams closed by result,
  stream duration, bytes to and from the backend, each stream accounted exactly once.
- Caddyfile and JSON config both expose the new options; document them.

Add integration tests in `caddytest/integration` that run a real server and real clients: streams
surviving and being closed across reloads in each mode, extended CONNECT over h2, upgrades through
`encode` and `intercept`, detached streams with access logging. Add unit tests for the pieces you
change. The existing suites must stay green. Do not change unrelated behaviour.

## Plan summary

One releasable change: add opt-in `stream_detached` plus a `stream_logs` block (skip_handshake, level) and stream metrics to reverse_proxy. Make the response-writer chain (recorder, encode, intercept) treat a 101 as final and write nothing after hijack. Detached streams are tracked in a package-level registry keyed by upstream and, on handler Cleanup, only those whose upstream is absent from the live config are closed. Docs are the Caddyfile doc comment and JSON field comments, since the repo has no separate docs tree.

## Task T1 (T1)

Order: (1) in caddyhttp, make responseRecorder treat 101 as final/unbuffered and no-op writes after Hijack; add the Server accessor for access loggers; (2) same hijack/101 hardening in encode and intercept; (3) add reverseproxy streams registry (package-level, keyed by upstream dial, live-upstream refcount maintained in Provision/Cleanup), StreamDetached, StreamLogs{SkipHandshake, Level} fields, Caddyfile parsing, and cleanupConnections branching (detached: close only streams whose upstream is no longer live; default path unchanged); (4) rewrite handleUpgradeResponse to account each stream once via a single finalizer (metrics, close log to access loggers) and set LogSkipVar when skip_handshake; (5) add metrics; (6) tests and caddyfile_adapt fixture, then docs in comments.

Acceptance criteria:
- ACC1 [behavior]: With stream_detached set, an upgraded stream stays open after a reload whose config still contains its upstream, and is closed after a reload that removes that upstream.
- ACC2 [behavior]: Caddyfile `stream_detached` and JSON `stream_detached: true` both set Handler.StreamDetached; it defaults to false.
- ACC3 [behavior]: Without stream_detached, an upgraded stream is closed on reload immediately, or after stream_close_delay when configured.
- ACC4 [behavior]: stream_logs { skip_handshake } parses in Caddyfile and JSON; when set the handshake request is not access-logged, by default it is.
- ACC5 [behavior]: A stream close log entry is written to the access logger (selectable with logger_name access) at the configured level, DEBUG by default, including after the config that created it was reloaded in detached mode.
- ACC6 [behavior]: ResponseRecorder, encode and intercept treat a 101 as the final response, never buffer it, and perform no header or body writes after Hijack; the proxy copies on the raw connection.
- ACC7 [behavior]: WebSocket/Upgrade streams work end to end through encode and through intercept with handle_response, with access logging enabled.
- ACC8 [behavior]: An HTTP/2 extended CONNECT websocket through reverse_proxy relays data, and an HTTP/1.1 upgrade works with stream_detached.
- ACC9 [behavior]: Metrics for active streams, closed-by-result, duration, and bytes to/from the backend are updated exactly once per stream, and the active gauge returns to zero.
- ACC10 [other]: Caddyfile syntax comment and JSON field comments document stream_detached, stream_logs, skip_handshake and the log level.
- ACC11 [behavior]: Integration tests exist for reload survive/close in each mode, extended CONNECT over h2, upgrades through encode and intercept, and detached streams with access logging.
- ACC12 [behavior]: Unit tests cover each changed unit (recorder, encode, intercept, registry/cleanup, metrics, caddyfile parsing).

diff --git a/caddytest/integration/stream_reload_test.go b/caddytest/integration/stream_reload_test.go
new file mode 100644
index 00000000..b5261797
--- /dev/null
+++ b/caddytest/integration/stream_reload_test.go
@@ -0,0 +1,227 @@
+package integration
+
+import (
+	"bufio"
+	"errors"
+	"fmt"
+	"io"
+	"net"
+	"net/http"
+	"sync"
+	"testing"
+	"time"
+
+	"github.com/caddyserver/caddy/v2/caddytest"
+)
+
+// streamBackend is an HTTP server that switches protocols on any request
+// that carries an Upgrade header, and echoes the stream afterwards. Other
+// requests get a plain response.
+type streamBackend struct {
+	addr  string
+	mu    sync.Mutex
+	conns []net.Conn
+}
+
+func startStreamBackend(t *testing.T) *streamBackend {
+	t.Helper()
+	ln, err := net.Listen("tcp", "127.0.0.1:0")
+	if err != nil {
+		t.Fatalf("starting the backend: %v", err)
+	}
+	b := &streamBackend{addr: ln.Addr().String()}
+	srv := &http.Server{Handler: http.HandlerFunc(b.serve)}
+	go srv.Serve(ln)
+	t.Cleanup(func() {
+		srv.Close()
+		b.mu.Lock()
+		defer b.mu.Unlock()
+		for _, c := range b.conns {
+			c.Close()
+		}
+	})
+	return b
+}
+
+func (b *streamBackend) serve(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
+	upgrade := r.Header.Get("Upgrade")
+	if upgrade == "" {
+		fmt.Fprint(w, "backend")
+		return
+	}
+	conn, brw, err := http.NewResponseController(w).Hijack()
+	if err != nil {
+		return
+	}
+	b.mu.Lock()
+	b.conns = append(b.conns, conn)
+	b.mu.Unlock()
+	defer conn.Close()
+
+	fmt.Fprintf(brw, "HTTP/1.1 101 Switching Protocols\r\nConnection: Upgrade\r\nUpgrade: %s\r\n\r\n", upgrade)
+	if brw.Flush() != nil {
+		return
+	}
+	io.Copy(conn, brw.Reader)
+}
+
+// streamClient is the client side of an upgraded HTTP/1.1 connection.
+type streamClient struct {
+	conn net.Conn
+	br   *bufio.Reader
+	resp *http.Response
+}
+
+// dialStream performs an upgrade handshake against the server listening on
+// port 9080 and fails the test if the response is not a 101.
+func dialStream(t *testing.T, path, upgrade string, header http.Header) *streamClient {
+	t.Helper()
+	conn, err := net.DialTimeout("tcp", "127.0.0.1:9080", 5*time.Second)
+	if err != nil {
+		t.Fatalf("dialing the server: %v", err)
+	}
+	t.Cleanup(func() { conn.Close() })
+
+	req, err := http.NewRequest(http.MethodGet, "http://localhost:9080"+path, nil)
+	if err != nil {
+		t.Fatal(err)
+	}
+	req.Header.Set("Connection", "Upgrade")
+	req.Header.Set("Upgrade", upgrade)
+	for k, v := range header {
+		req.Header[k] = v
+	}
+	if err := req.Write(conn); err != nil {
+		t.Fatalf("writing the upgrade request: %v", err)
+	}
+
+	br := bufio.NewReader(conn)
+	conn.SetReadDeadline(time.Now().Add(5 * time.Second))
+	resp, err := http.ReadResponse(br, req)
+	if err != nil {
+		t.Fatalf("reading the upgrade response: %v", err)
+	}
+	conn.SetReadDeadline(time.Time{})
+	if resp.StatusCode != http.StatusSwitchingProtocols {
+		t.Fatalf("upgrade status = %d, want 101", resp.StatusCode)
+	}
+	return &streamClient{conn: conn, br: br, resp: resp}
+}
+
+// echo sends msg through the stream and expects it back.
+func (c *streamClient) echo(msg string) error {
+	c.conn.SetDeadline(time.Now().Add(5 * time.Second))
+	defer c.conn.SetDeadline(time.Time{})
+	if _, err := io.WriteString(c.conn, msg); err != nil {
+		return err
+	}
+	buf := make([]byte, len(msg))
+	if _, err := io.ReadFull(c.br, buf); err != nil {
+		return err
+	}
+	if string(buf) != msg {
+		return fmt.Errorf("echoed %q, want %q", buf, msg)
+	}
+	return nil
+}
+
+// waitClosed reports whether the server closed the stream within d.
+func (c *streamClient) waitClosed(d time.Duration) bool {
+	c.conn.SetReadDeadline(time.Now().Add(d))
+	defer c.conn.SetReadDeadline(time.Time{})
+	_, err := io.Copy(io.Discard, c.br)
+	var netErr net.Error
+	return !(errors.As(err, &netErr) && netErr.Timeout())
+}
+
+// streamSite returns the config of a server that proxies to upstream, with
+// the given reverse_proxy options and extra site directives. A reload is
+// done by loading the config again with different extra directives.
+func streamSite(upstream, proxyOptions, extra string) string {
+	return fmt.Sprintf(`{
+		skip_install_trust
+		admin localhost:2999
+		http_port     9080
+		https_port    9443
+		grace_period  1ns
+	}
+
+	localhost:9080 {
+		%s
+		reverse_proxy %s {
+			%s
+		}
+	}`, extra, upstream, proxyOptions)
+}
+
+// By default, an upgraded stream is closed when the config is reloaded.
+func TestStreamIsClosedOnReload(t *testing.T) {
+	tester := caddytest.NewTester(t)
+	backend := startStreamBackend(t)
+
+	tester.InitServer(streamSite(backend.addr, "", `respond /version "v1"`), "caddyfile")
+	c := dialStream(t, "/ws", "echo", nil)
+	if err := c.echo("before"); err != nil {
+		t.Fatalf("echo before the reload: %v", err)
+	}
+
+	tester.InitServer(streamSite(backend.addr, "", `respond /version "v2"`), "caddyfile")
+	if !c.waitClosed(5 * time.Second) {
+		t.Fatal("the stream is still open after the reload")
+	}
+	tester.AssertGetResponse("http://localhost:9080/version", 200, "v2")
+}
+
+// With stream_close_delay, the stream outlives the reload until the delay is over.
+func TestStreamIsClosedAfterCloseDelay(t *testing.T) {
+	tester := caddytest.NewTester(t)
+	backend := startStreamBackend(t)
+
+	options := "stream_close_delay 1500ms"
+	tester.InitServer(streamSite(backend.addr, options, `respond /version "v1"`), "caddyfile")
+	c := dialStream(t, "/ws", "echo", nil)
+	if err := c.echo("before"); err != nil {
+		t.Fatalf("echo before the reload: %v", err)
+	}
+
+	reloaded := time.Now()
+	tester.InitServer(streamSite(backend.addr, options, `respond /version "v2"`), "caddyfile")
+	if err := c.echo("during the delay"); err != nil {
+		t.Fatalf("the stream should stay open during the close delay: %v", err)
+	}
+	if !c.waitClosed(5 * time.Second) {
+		t.Fatal("the stream is still open after the close delay")
+	}
+	if elapsed := time.Since(reloaded); elapsed < time.Second {
+		t.Errorf("the stream was closed %v after the reload, want it to wait for the delay", elapsed)
+	}
+}
+
+// A detached stream survives reloads that keep its upstream, and is closed
+// by the reload that removes it.
+func TestDetachedStreamFollowsItsUpstream(t *testing.T) {
+	tester := caddytest.NewTester(t)
+	backend := startStreamBackend(t)
+	otherBackend := startStreamBackend(t)
+	const options = "stream_detached"
+
+	tester.InitServer(streamSite(backend.addr, options, `respond /version "v1"`), "caddyfile")
+	c := dialStream(t, "/ws", "echo", nil)
+	if err := c.echo("before"); err != nil {
+		t.Fatalf("echo before the reload: %v", err)
+	}
+
+	tester.InitServer(streamSite(backend.addr, options, `respond /version "v2"`), "caddyfile")
+	tester.AssertGetResponse("http://localhost:9080/version", 200, "v2")
+	if c.waitClosed(time.Second) {
+		t.Fatal("the detached stream was closed by a reload that keeps its upstream")
+	}
+	if err := c.echo("after"); err != nil {
+		t.Fatalf("echo after the reload: %v", err)
+	}
+
+	tester.InitServer(streamSite(otherBackend.addr, options, `respond /version "v3"`), "caddyfile")
+	if !c.waitClosed(5 * time.Second) {
+		t.Fatal("the detached stream is still open after its upstream was removed")
+	}
+}
diff --git a/caddytest/integration/stream_upgrade_test.go b/caddytest/integration/stream_upgrade_test.go
new file mode 100644
index 00000000..024f6f42
--- /dev/null
+++ b/caddytest/integration/stream_upgrade_test.go
@@ -0,0 +1,389 @@
+package integration
+
+import (
+	"bufio"
+	"bytes"
+	"crypto/tls"
+	"encoding/json"
+	"fmt"
+	"io"
+	"net"
+	"net/http"
+	"os"
+	"os/exec"
+	"strings"
+	"sync"
+	"testing"
+	"time"
+
+	"golang.org/x/net/http2"
+	"golang.org/x/net/http2/hpack"
+
+	"github.com/caddyserver/caddy/v2/caddytest"
+)
+
+// logSink collects the JSON log entries that a server sends to it with the
+// net log writer.
+type logSink struct {
+	addr    string
+	mu      sync.Mutex
+	entries []map[string]any
+}
+
+func startLogSink(t *testing.T) *logSink {
+	t.Helper()
+	ln, err := net.Listen("tcp", "127.0.0.1:0")
+	if err != nil {
+		t.Fatalf("starting the log sink: %v", err)
+	}
+	s := &logSink{addr: ln.Addr().String()}
+	t.Cleanup(func() { ln.Close() })
+	go func() {
+		for {
+			conn, err := ln.Accept()
+			if err != nil {
+				return
+			}
+			go s.read(conn)
+		}
+	}()
+	return s
+}
+
+func (s *logSink) read(conn net.Conn) {
+	defer conn.Close()
+	sc := bufio.NewScanner(conn)
+	sc.Buffer(nil, 1<<20)
+	for sc.Scan() {
+		var entry map[string]any
+		if json.Unmarshal(sc.Bytes(), &entry) != nil {
+			continue
+		}
+		s.mu.Lock()
+		s.entries = append(s.entries, entry)
+		s.mu.Unlock()
+	}
+}
+
+// find returns the first entry that match.
+func (s *logSink) find(match func(map[string]any) bool) map[string]any {
+	s.mu.Lock()
+	defer s.mu.Unlock()
+	for _, e := range s.entries {
+		if match(e) {
+			return e
+		}
+	}
+	return nil
+}
+
+func (s *logSink) waitFor(t *testing.T, what string, match func(map[string]any) bool) map[string]any {
+	t.Helper()
+	deadline := time.Now().Add(5 * time.Second)
+	for time.Now().Before(deadline) {
+		if e := s.find(match); e != nil {
+			return e
+		}
+		time.Sleep(20 * time.Millisecond)
+	}
+	s.mu.Lock()
+	defer s.mu.Unlock()
+	t.Fatalf("timed out waiting for %s; got entries: %v", what, s.entries)
+	return nil
+}
+
+func isStreamClosed(e map[string]any) bool { return e["msg"] == "stream closed" }
+
+func isHandledRequest(uri string) func(map[string]any) bool {
+	return func(e map[string]any) bool {
+		req, _ := e["request"].(map[string]any)
+		return e["msg"] == "handled request" && req != nil && req["uri"] == uri
+	}
+}
+
+// accessLogSite is a server that proxies to upstream and writes its access
+// logs, under the logger name "access", to the sink.
+func accessLogSite(upstream, sink, proxyOptions, extra string) string {
+	return fmt.Sprintf(`{
+		skip_install_trust
+		admin localhost:2999
+		http_port     9080
+		https_port    9443
+		grace_period  1ns
+	}
+
+	localhost:9080 {
+		log access {
+			output net %s
+			format json
+			level DEBUG
+		}
+		%s
+		reverse_proxy %s {
+			%s
+		}
+	}`, sink, extra, upstream, proxyOptions)
+}
+
+// A detached stream still writes its close entry to the access log after
+// the config that created it was reloaded; the handshake is logged by default.
+func TestDetachedStreamCloseLogAfterReload(t *testing.T) {
+	tester := caddytest.NewTester(t)
+	backend := startStreamBackend(t)
+	sink := startLogSink(t)
+	const options = "stream_detached"
+
+	tester.InitServer(accessLogSite(backend.addr, sink.addr, options, `respond /version "v1"`), "caddyfile")
+	c := dialStream(t, "/ws", "echo", nil)
+	if err := c.echo("hello"); err != nil {
+		t.Fatalf("echo before the reload: %v", err)
+	}
+
+	tester.InitServer(accessLogSite(backend.addr, sink.addr, options, `respond /version "v2"`), "caddyfile")
+	tester.AssertGetResponse("http://localhost:9080/version", 200, "v2")
+	if err := c.echo("world"); err != nil {
+		t.Fatalf("echo after the reload: %v", err)
+	}
+	c.conn.Close()
+
+	closed := sink.waitFor(t, "the stream close entry", isStreamClosed)
+	if closed["logger"] != "http.log.access.access" {
+		t.Errorf("logger = %v, want http.log.access.access", closed["logger"])
+	}
+	if closed["level"] != "debug" {
+		t.Errorf("level = %v, want debug", closed["level"])
+	}
+	if closed["result"] != "completed" {
+		t.Errorf("result = %v, want completed", closed["result"])
+	}
+	if toBackend, _ := closed["bytes_to_backend"].(float64); toBackend != float64(len("helloworld")) {
+		t.Errorf("bytes_to_backend = %v, want %d", closed["bytes_to_backend"], len("helloworld"))
+	}
+	if fromBackend, _ := closed["bytes_from_backend"].(float64); fromBackend != float64(len("helloworld")) {
+		t.Errorf("bytes_from_backend = %v, want %d", closed["bytes_from_backend"], len("helloworld"))
+	}
+	if closed["upstream"] != backend.addr {
+		t.Errorf("upstream = %v, want %s", closed["upstream"], backend.addr)
+	}
+
+	// the handshake is logged unless told otherwise
+	sink.waitFor(t, "the handshake request entry", isHandledRequest("/ws"))
+}
+
+// With skip_handshake, the handshake is not access-logged, and the close
+// entry is written at the configured level.
+func TestStreamLogsSkipHandshake(t *testing.T) {
+	tester := caddytest.NewTester(t)
+	backend := startStreamBackend(t)
+	sink := startLogSink(t)
+
+	options := `stream_logs {
+		skip_handshake
+		level warn
+	}`
+	tester.InitServer(accessLogSite(backend.addr, sink.addr, options, ""), "caddyfile")
+	c := dialStream(t, "/ws", "echo", nil)
+	if err := c.echo("hello"); err != nil {
+		t.Fatalf("echo: %v", err)
+	}
+	c.conn.Close()
+
+	closed := sink.waitFor(t, "the stream close entry", isStreamClosed)
+	if closed["level"] != "warn" {
+		t.Errorf("level = %v, want warn", closed["level"])
+	}
+

+func TestExtendedConnectWebsocketOverH2(t *testing.T) {
+	if testing.Short() {
+		t.Skip("integration test")

+		// os.Args is rewritten when the tests start the server in-process
+		exe, err := os.Executable()
+		if err != nil {
+			t.Fatal(err)
+		}
+		cmd := exec.Command(exe,"-test.run=^TestExtendedConnectWebsocketOverH2$", "-test.count=1", "-test.timeout=2m")
+		cmd.Env = append(os.Environ(), "GODEBUG=http2xconnect=1")
+		if out, err := cmd.CombinedOutput(); err != nil {
+			t.Fatalf("test process failed: %v\n%s", err, out)

+		skip_install_trust
+		admin localhost:2998
+		http_port     9580
+		https_port    9543
+		grace_period  1ns
+	}

+		InsecureSkipVerify: true, //nolint:gosec
+		ServerName:         "localhost",
+		NextProtos:         []string{"h2"},
+	})

+		t.Fatal(err)
+	}
+	fr := http2.NewFramer(conn, conn)
+	if err := fr.WriteSettings(); err != nil {
+		t.Fatal(err)
+	}

+	var (
+		connectAllowed bool
+		status         string
+		data           []byte

+	decoder := hpack.NewDecoder(4096, func(f hpack.HeaderField) {
+		if f.Name == ":status" {

+	readFrames := func(done func() bool) {
+		t.Helper()

+			frame, err := fr.ReadFrame()
+			if err != nil {

+	encoder := hpack.NewEncoder(&block)
+	for _, f := range [][2]string{
+		{":method", "CONNECT"},
+		{":protocol", "websocket"},
+		{":scheme", "https"},
+		{":path", "/ws"},
+		{":authority", "localhost:9543"},
+		{"sec-websocket-version", "13"},
+	} {
+		if err := encoder.WriteField(hpack.HeaderField{Name: f[0], Value: f[1]}); err != nil {
+			t.Fatal(err)
+		}
+	}
+	err = fr.WriteHeaders(http2.HeadersFrameParam{StreamID: 1, BlockFragment: block.Bytes(), EndHeaders: true})
+	if err != nil {
+		t.Fatal(err)
+	}
+
+	readFrames(func() bool { return status != "" })
+	if status != "200" {
+		t.Fatalf("status = %s, want 200", status)
+	}
+
+	for _, msg := range []string{"hello over h2", "and again"} {
+		data = nil
+		if err := fr.WriteData(1, false, []byte(msg)); err != nil {
+			t.Fatalf("writing to the stream: %v", err)
+		}
+		readFrames(func() bool { return len(data) >= len(msg) })
+		if string(data) != msg {
+			t.Errorf("echoed %q, want %q", data, msg)
+		}
+	}
+}

+package reverseproxy

+// streamMetricsSnapshot is the state of the stream metrics at some point.
+type streamMetricsSnapshot struct {
+	active        float64

+	fromBackend   float64
+}
+
+// snapshotStreamMetrics reads the stream metrics through a registry, the way
+// a scrape would.
+func snapshotStreamMetrics(t *testing.T) streamMetricsSnapshot {
+	t.Helper()
+	registry := prometheus.NewRegistry()
+	initReverseProxyMetrics(&Handler{logger: zap.NewNop()}, registry)
+	families, err := registry.Gather()
+	if err != nil {
+		t.Fatalf("gathering metrics: %v", err)
+	}
+
+	snap := streamMetricsSnapshot{closed: make(map[string]float64)}
+	for _, mf := range families {
+		for _, m := range mf.GetMetric() {
+			switch mf.GetName() {
+			case "caddy_reverse_proxy_streams_active":
+				snap.active = m.GetGauge().GetValue()
+			case "caddy_reverse_proxy_streams_closed_total":
+				for _, l := range m.GetLabel() {
+					if l.GetName() == "result" {
+						snap.closed[l.GetValue()] = m.GetCounter().GetValue()
+					}
+				}
+			case "caddy_reverse_proxy_stream_duration_seconds":
+				snap.durationCount = m.GetHistogram().GetSampleCount()
+			case "caddy_reverse_proxy_stream_bytes_to_backend_total":
+				snap.toBackend = m.GetCounter().GetValue()
+			case "caddy_reverse_proxy_stream_bytes_from_backend_total":
+				snap.fromBackend = m.GetCounter().GetValue()
+			}
+		}
+	}
+	return snap

+func TestStreamMetricsAccountEachStreamOnce(t *testing.T) {
+	before := snapshotStreamMetrics(t)
+
+	streamStarted()
+	streamStarted()
+	during := snapshotStreamMetrics(t)
+	if got := during.active - before.active; got != 2 {
+		t.Fatalf("active streams went up by %v, want 2", got)
+	}
+
+	streamFinished(streamResultCompleted, 2*time.Second, 10, 20)
+	streamFinished(streamResultTimeout, time.Second, 1, 2)
+	after := snapshotStreamMetrics(t)
+
+	if after.active != before.active {
+		t.Errorf("active gauge = %v, want it back to %v", after.active, before.active)
+	}
+	if got := after.closed[streamResultCompleted] - before.closed[streamResultCompleted]; got != 1 {
+		t.Errorf("completed streams went up by %v, want 1", got)
+	}
+	if got := after.closed[streamResultTimeout] - before.closed[streamResultTimeout]; got != 1 {

+	}

+	}

## Original request

Harden upgraded-stream handling in `reverse_proxy` across config reloads (caddyserver/caddy
PR #7649 scope).

Long-lived upgraded connections through the reverse proxy (WebSocket and other `Upgrade`
tunnels, HTTP/2 extended CONNECT) keep the whole handler and config alive across reloads, so a
server that reloads often holds on to old configs, and the current behaviour on reload (close every
upgraded stream, optionally after a delay) is the only option. Middleware and response writers also
misbehave once a connection has been hijacked, and operators cannot see what their streams are
doing.

Required behaviour:

- A new opt-in `reverse_proxy` setting, `stream_detached`: when set, upgraded streams are detached
  from the config lifecycle and survive a reload; on reload only the streams whose upstream was
  removed from the new config are closed. The default stays as today: upgraded streams are closed on
  reload, honouring the existing close-delay behaviour.
- A `stream_logs` block with a `skip_handshake` option to suppress access logging of the upgrade
  handshake (default: logged), with stream close logs available in the access log via
  `logger_name access`, and a configurable log level (default DEBUG).
- Upgraded streams must keep working through the other handlers of a route: `encode`, `intercept`
  with `handle_response`, access logging. Once a connection is hijacked, nothing may write to the
  response again; a 101 is the final response for an upgrade; the proxy copies bytes on the raw
  connection, not through the recording response writer.
- HTTP/2 extended CONNECT (RFC 8441) upgrades keep working, as do HTTP/1.1 upgrades in detached
  mode.
- Stream observability metrics in `reverse_proxy`: active streams, streams closed by result,
  stream duration, bytes to and from the backend, each stream accounted exactly once.
- Caddyfile and JSON config both expose the new options; document them.

Add integration tests in `caddytest/integration` that run a real server and real clients: streams
surviving and being closed across reloads in each mode, extended CONNECT over h2, upgrades through
`encode` and `intercept`, detached streams with access logging. Add unit tests for the pieces you
change. The existing suites must stay green. Do not change unrelated behaviour.

## Plan summary

One releasable change: add opt-in `stream_detached` plus a `stream_logs` block (skip_handshake, level) and stream metrics to reverse_proxy. Make the response-writer chain (recorder, encode, intercept) treat a 101 as final and write nothing after hijack. Detached streams are tracked in a package-level registry keyed by upstream and, on handler Cleanup, only those whose upstream is absent from the live config are closed. Docs are the Caddyfile doc comment and JSON field comments, since the repo has no separate docs tree.

## Task T1 (T1)

Order: (1) in caddyhttp, make responseRecorder treat 101 as final/unbuffered and no-op writes after Hijack; add the Server accessor for access loggers; (2) same hijack/101 hardening in encode and intercept; (3) add reverseproxy streams registry (package-level, keyed by upstream dial, live-upstream refcount maintained in Provision/Cleanup), StreamDetached, StreamLogs{SkipHandshake, Level} fields, Caddyfile parsing, and cleanupConnections branching (detached: close only streams whose upstream is no longer live; default path unchanged); (4) rewrite handleUpgradeResponse to account each stream once via a single finalizer (metrics, close log to access loggers) and set LogSkipVar when skip_handshake; (5) add metrics; (6) tests and caddyfile_adapt fixture, then docs in comments.

Acceptance criteria:
- ACC1 [behavior]: With stream_detached set, an upgraded stream stays open after a reload whose config still contains its upstream, and is closed after a reload that removes that upstream.
- ACC2 [behavior]: Caddyfile `stream_detached` and JSON `stream_detached: true` both set Handler.StreamDetached; it defaults to false.
- ACC3 [behavior]: Without stream_detached, an upgraded stream is closed on reload immediately, or after stream_close_delay when configured.
- ACC4 [behavior]: stream_logs { skip_handshake } parses in Caddyfile and JSON; when set the handshake request is not access-logged, by default it is.
- ACC5 [behavior]: A stream close log entry is written to the access logger (selectable with logger_name access) at the configured level, DEBUG by default, including after the config that created it was reloaded in detached mode.
- ACC6 [behavior]: ResponseRecorder, encode and intercept treat a 101 as the final response, never buffer it, and perform no header or body writes after Hijack; the proxy copies on the raw connection.

+package integration

+// streamBackend is an HTTP server that switches protocols on any request
+// that carries an Upgrade header, and echoes the stream afterwards. Other
+// requests get a plain response.
+type streamBackend struct {
+	addr  string
+	mu    sync.Mutex
+	conns []net.Conn
+}
+
+func startStreamBackend(t *testing.T) *streamBackend {
+	t.Helper()
+	ln, err := net.Listen("tcp", "127.0.0.1:0")
+	if err != nil {
+		t.Fatalf("starting the backend: %v", err)
+	}
+	b := &streamBackend{addr: ln.Addr().String()}
+	srv := &http.Server{Handler: http.HandlerFunc(b.serve)}
+	go srv.Serve(ln)
+	t.Cleanup(func() {
+		srv.Close()
+		b.mu.Lock()
+		defer b.mu.Unlock()
+		for _, c := range b.conns {
+			c.Close()
+		}
+	})
+	return b
+}
+
+func (b *streamBackend) serve(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
+	upgrade := r.Header.Get("Upgrade")
+	if upgrade == "" {
+		fmt.Fprint(w, "backend")
+		return
+	}
+	conn, brw, err := http.NewResponseController(w).Hijack()
+	if err != nil {
+		return
+	}
+	b.mu.Lock()
+	b.conns = append(b.conns, conn)
+	b.mu.Unlock()
+	defer conn.Close()
+
+	fmt.Fprintf(brw, "HTTP/1.1 101 Switching Protocols\r\nConnection: Upgrade\r\nUpgrade: %s\r\n\r\n", upgrade)
+	if brw.Flush() != nil {
+		return
+	}
+	io.Copy(conn, brw.Reader)
+}
+
+// streamClient is the client side of an upgraded HTTP/1.1 connection.
+type streamClient struct {
+	conn net.Conn
+	br   *bufio.Reader
+	resp *http.Response
+}
+
+// dialStream performs an upgrade handshake against the server listening on
+// port 9080 and fails the test if the response is not a 101.
+func dialStream(t *testing.T, path, upgrade string, header http.Header) *streamClient {
+	t.Helper()
+	conn, err := net.DialTimeout("tcp", "127.0.0.1:9080", 5*time.Second)
+	if err != nil {
+		t.Fatalf("dialing the server: %v", err)
+	}
+	t.Cleanup(func() { conn.Close() })
+
+	req, err := http.NewRequest(http.MethodGet, "http://localhost:9080"+path, nil)
+	if err != nil {
+		t.Fatal(err)
+	}
+	req.Header.Set("Connection", "Upgrade")
+	req.Header.Set("Upgrade", upgrade)
+	for k, v := range header {
+		req.Header[k] = v
+	}
+	if err := req.Write(conn); err != nil {
+		t.Fatalf("writing the upgrade request: %v", err)
+	}
+
+	br := bufio.NewReader(conn)
+	conn.SetReadDeadline(time.Now().Add(5 * time.Second))
+	resp, err := http.ReadResponse(br, req)
+	if err != nil {
+		t.Fatalf("reading the upgrade response: %v", err)
+	}
+	conn.SetReadDeadline(time.Time{})
+	if resp.StatusCode != http.StatusSwitchingProtocols {
+		t.Fatalf("upgrade status = %d, want 101", resp.StatusCode)
+	}
+	return &streamClient{conn: conn, br: br, resp: resp}

+// echo sends msg through the stream and expects it back.
+func (c *streamClient) echo(msg string) error {
+	c.conn.SetDeadline(time.Now().Add(5 * time.Second))
+	defer c.conn.SetDeadline(time.Time{})
+	if _, err := io.WriteString(c.conn, msg); err != nil {
+		return err
+	}
+	buf := make([]byte, len(msg))
+	if _, err := io.ReadFull(c.br, buf); err != nil {
+		return err
+	}
+	if string(buf) != msg {
+		return fmt.Errorf("echoed %q, want %q", buf, msg)
+	}
+	return nil
+}

+	c.conn.SetReadDeadline(time.Now().Add(d))

+	_, err := io.Copy(io.Discard, c.br)
+	var netErr net.Error

+// A detached stream survives reloads that keep its upstream, and is closed

+// logSink collects the JSON log entries that a server sends to it with the
+// net log writer.
+type logSink struct {
+	addr    string
+	mu      sync.Mutex
+	entries []map[string]any
+}
+
+func startLogSink(t *testing.T) *logSink {
+	t.Helper()
+	ln, err := net.Listen("tcp", "127.0.0.1:0")
+	if err != nil {
+		t.Fatalf("starting the log sink: %v", err)
+	}
+	s := &logSink{addr: ln.Addr().String()}
+	t.Cleanup(func() { ln.Close() })
+	go func() {
+		for {
+			conn, err := ln.Accept()
+			if err != nil {
+				return
+			}
+			go s.read(conn)
+		}
+	}()
+	return s
+}
+
+func (s *logSink) read(conn net.Conn) {
+	defer conn.Close()
+	sc := bufio.NewScanner(conn)
+	sc.Buffer(nil, 1<<20)
+	for sc.Scan() {
+		var entry map[string]any
+		if json.Unmarshal(sc.Bytes(), &entry) != nil {
+			continue
+		}
+		s.mu.Lock()
+		s.entries = append(s.entries, entry)
+		s.mu.Unlock()
+	}
+}
+
+// find returns the first entry that match.
+func (s *logSink) find(match func(map[string]any) bool) map[string]any {
+	s.mu.Lock()
+	defer s.mu.Unlock()
+	for _, e := range s.entries {
+		if match(e) {
+			return e
+		}
+	}
+	return nil
+}

+func (s *logSink) waitFor(t *testing.T, what string, match func(map[string]any) bool) map[string]any {
+	t.Helper()
+	deadline := time.Now().Add(5 * time.Second)
+	for time.Now().Before(deadline) {
+		if e := s.find(match); e != nil {
+			return e
+		}
+		time.Sleep(20 * time.Millisecond)
+	}
+	s.mu.Lock()
+	defer s.mu.Unlock()

+	return nil

+		if out, err := cmd.CombinedOutput(); err != nil {
+			t.Fatalf("test process failed: %v\n%s", err, out)
+		}

+		https_port    9543

+	conn, err := tls.Dial("tcp", "127.0.0.1:9543",&tls.Config{

+		ServerName:         "localhost",
+		NextProtos:         []string{"h2"},
+	})

+		t.Fatalf("dialing the server: %v", err)
+	}
+	defer conn.Close()
+	conn.SetDeadline(time.Now().Add(10 * time.Second))
+
+	if _, err := io.WriteString(conn, http2.ClientPreface); err != nil {
+		t.Fatal(err)
+	}
+	fr := http2.NewFramer(conn, conn)
+	if err := fr.WriteSettings(); err != nil {
+		t.Fatal(err)
+	}
+
+	var (
+		connectAllowed bool
+		status         string
+		data           []byte

+	decoder := hpack.NewDecoder(4096, func(f hpack.HeaderField) {
+		if f.Name == ":status" {

+	readFrames := func(done func() bool) {

+			if err != nil {

+			}

+					connectAllowed = true

+	encoder := hpack.NewEncoder(&block)
+	for _, f := range [][2]string{
+		{":method", "CONNECT"},
+		{":protocol", "websocket"},
+		{":scheme", "https"},
+		{":path", "/ws"},
+		{":authority", "localhost:9543"},
+		{"sec-websocket-version", "13"},
+	} {
+		if err := encoder.WriteField(hpack.HeaderField{Name: f[0], Value: f[1]}); err != nil {
+			t.Fatal(err)
+		}
+	}
+	err = fr.WriteHeaders(http2.HeadersFrameParam{StreamID: 1, BlockFragment: block.Bytes(), EndHeaders: true})
+	if err != nil {
+		t.Fatal(err)
+	}
+
+	readFrames(func() bool { return status != "" })
+	if status != "200" {
+		t.Fatalf("status = %s, want 200", status)
+	}
+
+	for _, msg := range []string{"hello over h2", "and again"} {
+		data = nil
+		if err := fr.WriteData(1, false, []byte(msg)); err != nil {
+			t.Fatalf("writing to the stream: %v", err)
+		}
+		readFrames(func() bool { return len(data) >= len(msg) })
+		if string(data) != msg {
+			t.Errorf("echoed %q, want %q", data, msg)
+		}
+	}
+}

# Caddy Project Guidelines

## Mission

**Every site on HTTPS.** Caddy is a security-first, modular, extensible server platform.

## Code Style

### Go Idioms

Follow [Go Code Review Comments](https://go.dev/wiki/CodeReviewComments):

- **Error flow**: Early return, indent error handling—not else blocks
  ```go
  if err != nil {
      return err
  }
  // normal code
  ```
- **Naming**: initialisms (`URL`, `HTTP`, `ID`—not `Url`, `Http`, `Id`)
- **Receiver names**: 1–2 letters reflecting type (`c` for `Client`, `h` for `Handler`)
- **Error strings**: Lowercase, no trailing punctuation (`"something failed"` not `"Something failed."`)
- **Doc comments**: Full sentences starting with the name being documented
  ```go
  // Handler serves HTTP requests for the file server.
  type Handler struct { ... }
  ```
- **Empty slices**: `var t []string` (nil slice), not `t := []string{}` (non-nil zero-length)
- **Don't panic**: Use error returns for normal error handling

### Caddy Patterns

**Module registration**:
```go
func init() {
    caddy.RegisterModule(MyModule{})

# Caddy Project Guidelines

## Mission

**Every site on HTTPS.** Caddy is a security-first, modular, extensible server platform.

## Code Style

### Go Idioms

Follow [Go Code Review Comments](https://go.dev/wiki/CodeReviewComments):

- **Error flow**: Early return, indent error handling—not else blocks
  ```go
  if err != nil {
      return err
  }
  // normal code
  ```
- **Naming**: initialisms (`URL`, `HTTP`, `ID`—not `Url`, `Http`, `Id`)
- **Receiver names**: 1–2 letters reflecting type (`c` for `Client`, `h` for `Handler`)
- **Error strings**: Lowercase, no trailing punctuation (`"something failed"` not `"Something failed."`)
- **Doc comments**: Full sentences starting with the name being documented
  ```go
  // Handler serves HTTP requests for the file server.
  type Handler struct { ... }
  ```
- **Empty slices**: `var t []string` (nil slice), not `t := []string{}` (non-nil zero-length)
- **Don't panic**: Use error returns for normal error handling

### Caddy Patterns

**Module registration**:
```go
func init() {
    caddy.RegisterModule(MyModule{})
}

func (MyModule) CaddyModule() caddy.ModuleInfo {
    return caddy.ModuleInfo{
        ID:  "namespace.category.name",
        New: func() caddy.Module { return new(MyModule) },
    }
}
```

**Module lifecycle**: `New()` → JSON unmarshal → `Provision()` → `Validate()` → use → `Cleanup()`

**Interface guards** — compile-time verification that modules implement required interfaces:
```go
var (
    _ caddy.Provisioner     = (*MyModule)(nil)
    _ caddy.Validator       = (*MyModule)(nil)
    _ caddyfile.Unmarshaler = (*MyModule)(nil)
)
```

**Structured logging** — use the module-scoped logger from context:
```go
func (m *MyModule) Provision(ctx caddy.Context) error {
    m.logger = ctx.Logger()
    m.logger.Debug("provisioning", zap.String("field", m.Field))
    return nil
}
```

**Caddyfile support** — implement `UnmarshalCaddyfile(*caddyfile.Dispenser)` using the `Dispenser` API:
```go
// UnmarshalCaddyfile sets up the module from Caddyfile tokens. Syntax:
//
//     directive [arg1] [arg2] {
//         subdir value
//     }
func (m *MyModule) UnmarshalCaddyfile(d *caddyfile.Dispenser) error {
    d.Next() // consume directive name
    for d.NextArg() {
        // handle inline arguments
    }
    for nesting := d.Nesting(); d.NextBlock(nesting); {
        switch d.Val() {
        case "subdir":
            if !d.NextArg() {
                return d.ArgErr()
            }
            m.Field = d.Val()
        default:
            return d.Errf("unrecognized subdirective: %s", d.Val())
        }
    }
    return nil
}
```

**Admin API**: Implement `caddy.AdminRouter` for custom endpoints.

**Context**: Use `caddy.Context` for accessing other apps/modules and logging—don't store contexts in structs.

## Architecture

Caddy is built around a **module system** where everything is a module registered via `caddy.RegisterModule()`:

- **Apps** (`caddy.App`): Top-level modules like `http`, `tls`, `pki` that Caddy loads and runs
- **Modules** (`caddy.Module`): Extensible components with namespaced IDs (e.g., `http.handlers.file_server`)
- **Configuration**: Native JSON with adapters (Caddyfile → JSON via `caddyconfig/httpcaddyfile`)

| Directory | Purpose |
|-----------|---------|
| `modules/` | All standard modules (HTTP, TLS, PKI, etc.) |
| `modules/standard/imports.go` | Standard module registry |
| `caddyconfig/httpcaddyfile/` | Caddyfile → JSON adapter for HTTP |
| `caddytest/` | Test utilities and integration tests |
| `cmd/caddy/` | CLI entry point with module imports |

### Critical Packages

`caddyhttp` and `caddytls` require **extra scrutiny** in code review—these are security-critical.

Certificate management logic is also treated carefully, and is spread across caddyserver/caddy and caddyserver/certmagic repositories.

## Quality Gates


**All required before PR is merge-ready:**

| Gate | Command | Notes |
|------|---------|-------|
| Tests pass | `go test -race -short ./...` | Race detection enabled |
| Lint clean | `golangci-lint run --timeout 10m` | No warnings in changed files |
| Builds | `go build ./...` | Must compile |
| Benchmarks | `go test -bench=. -benchmem` | Required for optimizations |

CI runs tests on **Linux, macOS, and Windows**—ensure cross-platform compatibility.

### Build & Test

```bash
# Build
cd cmd/caddy && go build

# Tests with race detection (matches CI)
go test -race -short ./...

# Integration tests
go test ./caddytest/integration/...

# Lint (matches CI)
golangci-lint run --timeout 10m
```

## Testing Conventions

**Table-driven tests** (preferred pattern):
```go
func TestFeature(t *testing.T) {
    for i, tc := range []struct {
        input    string
        expected string
        wantErr  bool
    }{
        {input: "valid", expected: "result", wantErr: false},
        {input: "invalid", expected: "", wantErr: true},
    } {
        actual, err := Function(tc.input)
        if tc.wantErr && err == nil {
            t.Errorf("Test %d: expected error but got none", i)
        }
        if !tc.wantErr && err != nil {
            t.Errorf("Test %d: unexpected error: %v", i, err)
        }
        if actual != tc.expected {
            t.Errorf("Test %d: expected %q, got %q", i, tc.expected, actual)
        }
    }
}
```

**Integration tests** use `caddytest.Tester`:
```go
func TestHTTPFeature(t *testing.T) {
    tester := caddytest.NewTester(t)
    tester.InitServer(`
    {
        admin localhost:2999
        http_port 9080
    }
    localhost:9080 {
        respond "hello"
    }`, "caddyfile")
    
    tester.AssertGetResponse("http://localhost:9080/", 200, "hello")
}
```

Use non-standard ports (9080, 9443, 2999) to avoid conflicts with running servers.

## Original request

Harden upgraded-stream handling in `reverse_proxy` across config reloads (caddyserver/caddy
PR #7649 scope).

Long-lived upgraded connections through the reverse proxy (WebSocket and other `Upgrade`
tunnels, HTTP/2 extended CONNECT) keep the whole handler and config alive across reloads, so a
server that reloads often holds on to old configs, and the current behaviour on reload (close every
upgraded stream, optionally after a delay) is the only option. Middleware and response writers also
misbehave once a connection has been hijacked, and operators cannot see what their streams are
doing.

Required behaviour:

- A new opt-in `reverse_proxy` setting, `stream_detached`: when set, upgraded streams are detached
  from the config lifecycle and survive a reload; on reload only the streams whose upstream was
  removed from the new config are closed. The default stays as today: upgraded streams are closed on
  reload, honouring the existing close-delay behaviour.
- A `stream_logs` block with a `skip_handshake` option to suppress access logging of the upgrade
  handshake (default: logged), with stream close logs available in the access log via
  `logger_name access`, and a configurable log level (default DEBUG).
- Upgraded streams must keep working through the other handlers of a route: `encode`, `intercept`
  with `handle_response`, access logging. Once a connection is hijacked, nothing may write to the
  response again; a 101 is the final response for an upgrade; the proxy copies bytes on the raw
  connection, not through the recording response writer.
- HTTP/2 extended CONNECT (RFC 8441) upgrades keep working, as do HTTP/1.1 upgrades in detached
  mode.
- Stream observability metrics in `reverse_proxy`: active streams, streams closed by result,
  stream duration, bytes to and from the backend, each stream accounted exactly once.
- Caddyfile and JSON config both expose the new options; document them.

Add integration tests in `caddytest/integration` that run a real server and real clients: streams
surviving and being closed across reloads in each mode, extended CONNECT over h2, upgrades through
`encode` and `intercept`, detached streams with access logging. Add unit tests for the pieces you
change. The existing suites must stay green. Do not change unrelated behaviour.

+// streamBackend is an HTTP server that switches protocols on any request
+// that carries an Upgrade header, and echoes the stream afterwards. Other
+// requests get a plain response.
+type streamBackend struct {
+	addr  string
+	mu    sync.Mutex
+	conns []net.Conn
+}
+
+func startStreamBackend(t *testing.T) *streamBackend {
+	t.Helper()
+	ln, err := net.Listen("tcp", "127.0.0.1:0")
+	if err != nil {
+		t.Fatalf("starting the backend: %v", err)
+	}
+	b := &streamBackend{addr: ln.Addr().String()}
+	srv := &http.Server{Handler: http.HandlerFunc(b.serve)}
+	go srv.Serve(ln)
+	t.Cleanup(func() {
+		srv.Close()
+		b.mu.Lock()
+		defer b.mu.Unlock()
+		for _, c := range b.conns {
+			c.Close()
+		}
+	})
+	return b
+}
+
+func (b *streamBackend) serve(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
+	upgrade := r.Header.Get("Upgrade")
+	if upgrade == "" {
+		fmt.Fprint(w, "backend")
+		return
+	}
+	conn, brw, err := http.NewResponseController(w).Hijack()
+	if err != nil {
+		return
+	}
+	b.mu.Lock()
+	b.conns = append(b.conns, conn)
+	b.mu.Unlock()
+	defer conn.Close()
+
+	fmt.Fprintf(brw, "HTTP/1.1 101 Switching Protocols\r\nConnection: Upgrade\r\nUpgrade: %s\r\n\r\n", upgrade)
+	if brw.Flush() != nil {
+		return
+	}
+	io.Copy(conn, brw.Reader)
+}
+
+// streamClient is the client side of an upgraded HTTP/1.1 connection.
+type streamClient struct {
+	conn net.Conn
+	br   *bufio.Reader
+	resp *http.Response
+}
+
+// dialStream performs an upgrade handshake against the server listening on
+// port 9080 and fails the test if the response is not a 101.
+func dialStream(t *testing.T, path, upgrade string, header http.Header) *streamClient {
+	t.Helper()
+	conn, err := net.DialTimeout("tcp", "127.0.0.1:9080", 5*time.Second)
+	if err != nil {
+		t.Fatalf("dialing the server: %v", err)
+	}
+	t.Cleanup(func() { conn.Close() })
+
+	req, err := http.NewRequest(http.MethodGet, "http://localhost:9080"+path, nil)
+	if err != nil {
+		t.Fatal(err)
+	}
+	req.Header.Set("Connection", "Upgrade")
+	req.Header.Set("Upgrade", upgrade)
+	for k, v := range header {
+		req.Header[k] = v
+	}
+	if err := req.Write(conn); err != nil {
+		t.Fatalf("writing the upgrade request: %v", err)
+	}
+
+	br := bufio.NewReader(conn)
+	conn.SetReadDeadline(time.Now().Add(5 * time.Second))
+	resp, err := http.ReadResponse(br, req)
+	if err != nil {
+		t.Fatalf("reading the upgrade response: %v", err)
+	}
+	conn.SetReadDeadline(time.Time{})
+	if resp.StatusCode != http.StatusSwitchingProtocols {
+		t.Fatalf("upgrade status = %d, want 101", resp.StatusCode)
+	}
+	return &streamClient{conn: conn, br: br, resp: resp}
+}
+
+// echo sends msg through the stream and expects it back.
+func (c *streamClient) echo(msg string) error {
+	c.conn.SetDeadline(time.Now().Add(5 * time.Second))
+	defer c.conn.SetDeadline(time.Time{})
+	if _, err := io.WriteString(c.conn, msg); err != nil {
+		return err
+	}
+	buf := make([]byte, len(msg))
+	if _, err := io.ReadFull(c.br, buf); err != nil {
+		return err
+	}
+	if string(buf) != msg {
+		return fmt.Errorf("echoed %q, want %q", buf, msg)
+	}
+	return nil
+}
+
+// waitClosed reports whether the server closed the stream within d.
+func (c *streamClient) waitClosed(d time.Duration) bool {
+	c.conn.SetReadDeadline(time.Now().Add(d))
+	defer c.conn.SetReadDeadline(time.Time{})
+	_, err := io.Copy(io.Discard, c.br)
+	var netErr net.Error
+	return !(errors.As(err, &netErr) && netErr.Timeout())
+}

+// logSink collects the JSON log entries that a server sends to it with the
+// net log writer.
+type logSink struct {
+	addr    string
+	mu      sync.Mutex
+	entries []map[string]any
+}
+
+func startLogSink(t *testing.T) *logSink {
+	t.Helper()
+	ln, err := net.Listen("tcp", "127.0.0.1:0")
+	if err != nil {
+		t.Fatalf("starting the log sink: %v", err)
+	}
+	s := &logSink{addr: ln.Addr().String()}
+	t.Cleanup(func() { ln.Close() })
+	go func() {
+		for {
+			conn, err := ln.Accept()
+			if err != nil {
+				return
+			}
+			go s.read(conn)
+		}
+	}()
+	return s
+}
+
+func (s *logSink) read(conn net.Conn) {
+	defer conn.Close()
+	sc := bufio.NewScanner(conn)
+	sc.Buffer(nil, 1<<20)
+	for sc.Scan() {
+		var entry map[string]any
+		if json.Unmarshal(sc.Bytes(), &entry) != nil {
+			continue
+		}
+		s.mu.Lock()
+		s.entries = append(s.entries, entry)
+		s.mu.Unlock()
+	}
+}
+
+// find returns the first entry that match.
+func (s *logSink) find(match func(map[string]any) bool) map[string]any {
+	s.mu.Lock()
+	defer s.mu.Unlock()
+	for _, e := range s.entries {
+		if match(e) {
+			return e
+		}
+	}
+	return nil
+}
+
+func (s *logSink) waitFor(t *testing.T, what string, match func(map[string]any) bool) map[string]any {
+	t.Helper()
+	deadline := time.Now().Add(5 * time.Second)
+	for time.Now().Before(deadline) {
+		if e := s.find(match); e != nil {
+			return e
+		}
+		time.Sleep(20 * time.Millisecond)
+	}
+	s.mu.Lock()
+	defer s.mu.Unlock()
+	t.Fatalf("timed out waiting for %s; got entries: %v", what, s.entries)
+	return nil
+}

+// backend that speaks the HTTP/1.1 upgrade.
+//
+// The server only advertises extended CONNECT support when the process runs
+// with GODEBUG=http2xconnect=1, which is read when the process starts. So

+// endpoint of its own so that it doesn't meet the server of this process.
+func TestExtendedConnectWebsocketOverH2(t *testing.T) {
+	if testing.Short() {
+		t.Skip("integration test")
+	}
+	if !strings.Contains(os.Getenv("GODEBUG"), "http2xconnect=1") {
+		// os.Args is rewritten when the tests start the server in-process
+		exe, err := os.Executable()
+		if err != nil {
+			t.Fatal(err)
+		}
+		cmd := exec.Command(exe,"-test.run=^TestExtendedConnectWebsocketOverH2$", "-test.count=1", "-test.timeout=2m")
+		cmd.Env = append(os.Environ(), "GODEBUG=http2xconnect=1")
+		if out, err := cmd.CombinedOutput(); err != nil {
+			t.Fatalf("test process failed: %v\n%s", err, out)
+		}
+		return
+	}
+
+	tester := caddytest.NewTester(t).WithDefaultOverrides(caddytest.Config{AdminPort: 2998})
+	backend := startStreamBackend(t)
+
+	config := fmt.Sprintf(`{
+		skip_install_trust
+		admin localhost:2998
+		http_port     9580
+		https_port    9543
+		grace_period  1ns
+	}
+
+	localhost:9543 {
+		reverse_proxy %s
+	}`, backend.addr)
+	tester.InitServer(config, "caddyfile")
+
+	// The HTTP/2 clients of the standard library don't send extended CONNECT
+	// requests, so speak the protocol directly.
+	conn, err := tls.Dial("tcp", "127.0.0.1:9543",&tls.Config{
+		InsecureSkipVerify: true, //nolint:gosec
+		ServerName:         "localhost",
+		NextProtos:         []string{"h2"},
+	})
+	if err != nil {
+		t.Fatalf("dialing the server: %v", err)
+	}
+	defer conn.Close()
+	conn.SetDeadline(time.Now().Add(10 * time.Second))
+
+	if _, err := io.WriteString(conn, http2.ClientPreface); err != nil {
+		t.Fatal(err)
+	}
+	fr := http2.NewFramer(conn, conn)
+	if err := fr.WriteSettings(); err != nil {
+		t.Fatal(err)
+	}
+
+	var (
+		connectAllowed bool
+		status         string
+		data           []byte
+	)
+	decoder := hpack.NewDecoder(4096, func(f hpack.HeaderField) {
+		if f.Name == ":status" {
+			status = f.Value
+		}
+	})
+	// readFrames handles the frames of the connection until done reports true
+	readFrames := func(done func() bool) {
+		t.Helper()
+		for !done() {
+			frame, err := fr.ReadFrame()
+			if err != nil {
+				t.Fatalf("reading a frame: %v", err)
+			}
+			switch f := frame.(type) {
+			case *http2.SettingsFrame:
+				if f.IsAck() {
+					continue

+				if v, ok := f.Value(http2.SettingID(0x8)); ok && v == 1 { // SETTINGS_ENABLE_CONNECT_PROTOCOL
+					connectAllowed = true

+				if err := fr.WriteSettingsAck(); err != nil {
+					t.Fatal(err)
+				}
+			case *http2.HeadersFrame:
+				if _, err := decoder.Write(f.HeaderBlockFragment()); err != nil {
+					t.Fatal(err)
+				}
+			case *http2.DataFrame:

+			case *http2.RSTStreamFrame:
+				t.Fatalf("the stream was reset: %v", f.ErrCode)
+			case *http2.GoAwayFrame:
+				t.Fatalf("the connection was closed: %v", f.ErrCode)
+			}
+		}
+	}
+
+	readFrames(func() bool { return connectAllowed })
+
+	var block bytes.Buffer
+	encoder := hpack.NewEncoder(&block)
+	for _, f := range [][2]string{
+		{":method", "CONNECT"},
+		{":protocol", "websocket"},
+		{":scheme", "https"},
+		{":path", "/ws"},
+		{":authority", "localhost:9543"},
+		{"sec-websocket-version", "13"},
+	} {
+		if err := encoder.WriteField(hpack.HeaderField{Name: f[0], Value: f[1]}); err != nil {
+			t.Fatal(err)
+		}
+	}
+	err = fr.WriteHeaders(http2.HeadersFrameParam{StreamID: 1, BlockFragment: block.Bytes(), EndHeaders: true})
+	if err != nil {
+		t.Fatal(err)
+	}
+
+	readFrames(func() bool { return status != "" })
+	if status != "200" {
+		t.Fatalf("status = %s, want 200", status)
+	}
+
+	for _, msg := range []string{"hello over h2", "and again"} {
+		data = nil
+		if err := fr.WriteData(1, false, []byte(msg)); err != nil {
+			t.Fatalf("writing to the stream: %v", err)
+		}
+		readFrames(func() bool { return len(data) >= len(msg) })
+		if string(data) != msg {
+			t.Errorf("echoed %q, want %q", data, msg)
+		}
+	}
+}

+package reverseproxy
+
+import (

+)

+// streamMetricsSnapshot is the state of the stream metrics at some point.
+type streamMetricsSnapshot struct {
+	active        float64
+	closed        map[string]float64
+	durationCount uint64
+	toBackend     float64
+	fromBackend   float64
+}
+
+// snapshotStreamMetrics reads the stream metrics through a registry, the way
+// a scrape would.
+func snapshotStreamMetrics(t *testing.T) streamMetricsSnapshot {
+	t.Helper()
+	registry := prometheus.NewRegistry()
+	initReverseProxyMetrics(&Handler{logger: zap.NewNop()}, registry)
+	families, err := registry.Gather()
+	if err != nil {
+		t.Fatalf("gathering metrics: %v", err)
+	}
+
+	snap := streamMetricsSnapshot{closed: make(map[string]float64)}
+	for _, mf := range families {
+		for _, m := range mf.GetMetric() {
+			switch mf.GetName() {
+			case "caddy_reverse_proxy_streams_active":
+				snap.active = m.GetGauge().GetValue()
+			case "caddy_reverse_proxy_streams_closed_total":
+				for _, l := range m.GetLabel() {
+					if l.GetName() == "result" {
+						snap.closed[l.GetValue()] = m.GetCounter().GetValue()
+					}
+				}
+			case "caddy_reverse_proxy_stream_duration_seconds":
+				snap.durationCount = m.GetHistogram().GetSampleCount()
+			case "caddy_reverse_proxy_stream_bytes_to_backend_total":
+				snap.toBackend = m.GetCounter().GetValue()
+			case "caddy_reverse_proxy_stream_bytes_from_backend_total":
+				snap.fromBackend = m.GetCounter().GetValue()
+			}
+		}
+	}
+	return snap
+}

+func TestStreamMetricsAccountEachStreamOnce(t *testing.T) {
+	before := snapshotStreamMetrics(t)
+
+	streamStarted()
+	streamStarted()
+	during := snapshotStreamMetrics(t)
+	if got := during.active - before.active; got != 2 {
+		t.Fatalf("active streams went up by %v, want 2", got)
+	}
+
+	streamFinished(streamResultCompleted, 2*time.Second, 10, 20)
+	streamFinished(streamResultTimeout, time.Second, 1, 2)
+	after := snapshotStreamMetrics(t)
+
+	if after.active != before.active {
+		t.Errorf("active gauge = %v, want it back to %v", after.active, before.active)
+	}
+	if got := after.closed[streamResultCompleted] - before.closed[streamResultCompleted]; got != 1 {
+		t.Errorf("completed streams went up by %v, want 1", got)
+	}
+	if got := after.closed[streamResultTimeout] - before.closed[streamResultTimeout]; got != 1 {
+		t.Errorf("timed out streams went up by %v, want 1", got)
+	}
+	if got := after.durationCount - before.durationCount; got != 2 {
+		t.Errorf("duration observations went up by %d, want 2", got)
+	}
+	if got := after.toBackend - before.toBackend; got != 11 {

+	}

- Filter with `glob` (e.g. "**/*.tsx") or `type` (e.g. "js", "py", "rust").
- `output_mode`: "content" (matching lines), "files_with_matches" (paths only, default), or "count".
- `multiline: true` for patterns that span lines.

pattern.description: The regular expression pattern to search for in file contents

path.description: File or directory to search in (rg PATH). Defaults to current working directory.

glob.description: Glob pattern to filter files (e.g. "*.js", "*.{ts,tsx}") - maps to rg --glob

output_mode.description: Output mode: "content" shows matching lines (supports -A/-B/-C context, -n line numbers, head_limit), "files_with_matches" shows file paths (supports head_limit), "count" shows match counts (supports head_limit). Defaults to "files_with_matches".

-B.description: Number of lines to show before each match (rg -B). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-A.description: Number of lines to show after each match (rg -A). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

context.description: Number of lines to show before and after each match (rg -C). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-n.description: Show line numbers in output (rg -n). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to true.

-o.description: Print only the matched (non-empty) parts of each matching line, one match per output line (rg -o / --only-matching). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to false.

type.description: File type to search (rg --type). Common types: js, py, rust, go, java, etc. More efficient than include for standard file types.

head_limit.description: Limit output to first N lines/entries, equivalent to "| head -N". Works across all output modes: content (limits output lines), files_with_matches (limits file paths), count (limits count entries). Defaults to 250 when unspecified. Pass 0 for unlimited (use sparingly — large result sets waste context).

offset.description: Skip first N lines/entries before applying head_limit, equivalent to "| tail -n +N | head -N". Works across all output modes. Defaults to 0.

multiline.description: Enable multiline mode where . matches newlines and patterns can span lines (rg -U --multiline-dotall). Default: false.

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

42	type h2ReadWriteCloser struct {
43		io.ReadCloser
44		http.ResponseWriter
45	}
46	
47	func (rwc h2ReadWriteCloser) Write(p []byte) (n int, err error) {
48		n, err = rwc.ResponseWriter.Write(p)
49		if err != nil {
50			return 0, err
51		}
52	
53		//nolint:bodyclose
54		err = http.NewResponseController(rwc.ResponseWriter).Flush()
55		if err != nil {
56			return 0, err
57		}
58		return n, nil
59	}
60	
61	func (h *Handler) handleUpgradeResponse(logger *zap.Logger, wg *sync.WaitGroup, rw http.ResponseWriter, req *http.Request, res *http.Response) {
62		reqUpType := upgradeType(req.Header)
63		resUpType := upgradeType(res.Header)
64	
65		// Taken from https://github.com/golang/go/commit/5c489514bc5e61ad9b5b07bd7d8ec65d66a0512a
66		// We know reqUpType is ASCII, it's checked by the caller.
67		if !asciiIsPrint(resUpType) {
68			if c := logger.Check(zapcore.DebugLevel, "backend tried to switch to invalid protocol"); c != nil {
69				c.Write(zap.String("backend_upgrade", resUpType))
70			}
71			return
72		}
73		if !asciiEqualFold(reqUpType, resUpType) {
74			if c := logger.Check(zapcore.DebugLevel, "backend tried to switch to unexpected protocol via Upgrade header"); c != nil {
75				c.Write(
76					zap.String("backend_upgrade", resUpType),
77					zap.String("requested_upgrade", reqUpType),
78				)
79			}
80			return
81		}
82	
83		backConn, ok := res.Body.(io.ReadWriteCloser)
84		if !ok {
85			logger.Error("internal error: 101 switching protocols response with non-writable body")
86			return
87		}
88	
89		if h.StreamLogs != nil && h.StreamLogs.SkipHandshake {
90			caddyhttp.SetVar(req.Context(), caddyhttp.LogSkipVar, true)
91		}
92	
93		// write header first, response headers should not be counted in size
94		// like the rest of handler chain.
95		copyHeader(rw.Header(), res.Header)
96		normalizeWebsocketHeaders(rw.Header())
97	
98		var (
99			conn io.ReadWriteCloser
100			brw  *bufio.ReadWriter
101		)
102		// websocket over http2 or http3 if extended connect is enabled, assuming backend doesn't support this, the request will be modified to http1.1 upgrade
103		// TODO: once we can reliably detect backend support this, it can be removed for those backends
104		if body, ok := caddyhttp.GetVar(req.Context(), "extended_connect_websocket_body").(io.ReadCloser); ok {
105			req.Body = body
106			rw.Header().Del("Upgrade")
107			rw.Header().Del("Connection")
108			delete(rw.Header(), "Sec-WebSocket-Accept")
109			rw.WriteHeader(http.StatusOK)
110	
111			if c := logger.Check(zap.DebugLevel, "upgrading connection"); c != nil {
112				c.Write(zap.Int("http_version", 2))
113			}
114	
115			//nolint:bodyclose
116			flushErr := http.NewResponseController(rw).Flush()
117			if flushErr != nil {
118				if c := h.logger.Check(zap.ErrorLevel, "failed to flush http2 websocket response"); c != nil {
119					c.Write(zap.Error(flushErr))
120				}
121				return
122			}
123			conn = h2ReadWriteCloser{req.Body, rw}
124			// bufio is not needed, use minimal buffer
125			brw = bufio.NewReadWriter(bufio.NewReaderSize(conn, 1), bufio.NewWriterSize(conn, 1))
126		} else {
127			rw.WriteHeader(res.StatusCode)
128	
129			if c := logger.Check(zap.DebugLevel, "upgrading connection"); c != nil {
130				c.Write(zap.Int("http_version", req.ProtoMajor))
131			}
132	
133			var hijackErr error
134			//nolint:bodyclose
135			conn, brw, hijackErr = http.NewResponseController(rw).Hijack()
136			if errors.Is(hijackErr, http.ErrNotSupported) {
137				if c := h.logger.Check(zap.ErrorLevel, "can't switch protocols using non-Hijacker ResponseWriter"); c != nil {
138					c.Write(zap.String("type", fmt.Sprintf("%T", rw)))
139				}
140				return
141			}
142	
143			if hijackErr != nil {
144				if c := h.logger.Check(zap.ErrorLevel, "hijack failed on protocol switch"); c != nil {
145					c.Write(zap.Error(hijackErr))
146				}
147				return
148			}
149		}
150	
151		// adopted from https://github.com/golang/go/commit/8bcf2834afdf6a1f7937390903a41518715ef6f5
152		backConnCloseCh := make(chan struct{})
153		go func() {
154			// Ensure that the cancellation of a request closes the backend.
155			// See issue https://golang.org/issue/35559.
156			select {
157			case <-req.Context().Done():
158			case <-backConnCloseCh:
159			}
160			backConn.Close()
161		}()
162	
163		// From here on the stream is open and accounted for. The deferred
164		// function below is the only place where it is accounted as closed, so
165		// each stream is counted exactly once whichever way it ends.
166		start := time.Now()
167		stream := &upgradedStream{upstream: streamUpstream(req)}
168		spc := &switchProtocolCopier{
169			user:       conn,
170			backend:    backConn,
171			wg:         wg,
172			bufferSize: h.StreamBufferSize,
173		}
174		result := streamResultCompleted
175		streamStarted()
176		defer func() {
177			close(backConnCloseCh)
178			conn.Close()
179			backConn.Close()
180			// let the copiers end so that the byte counts are final
181			wg.Wait()
182	
183			duration := time.Since(start)
184			switch {
185			case stream.closedByCleanup.Load():
186				result = streamResultReload
187			case result == streamResultError && req.Context().Err() != nil:
188				result = streamResultCanceled
189			}
190			toBackend, fromBackend := spc.bytesToBackend.Load(), spc.bytesFromBackend.Load()
191			streamFinished(result, duration, toBackend, fromBackend)
192	
193			if c := logger.Check(zapcore.DebugLevel, "connection closed"); c != nil {
194				c.Write(zap.Duration("duration", duration))
195			}
196			h.logStreamClosed(req, stream, result, duration, toBackend, fromBackend)
197		}()
198	
199		if err := brw.Flush(); err != nil {
200			if c := logger.Check(zapcore.DebugLevel, "response flush"); c != nil {
201				c.Write(zap.Error(err))
202			}
203			result = streamResultError
204			return
205		}
206	
207		// There may be buffered data in the *bufio.Reader
208		// see: https://github.com/caddyserver/caddy/issues/6273
209		if buffered := brw.Reader.Buffered(); buffered > 0 {
210			data, _ := brw.Peek(buffered)
211			n, err := backConn.Write(data)
212			spc.bytesToBackend.Add(int64(n))
213			if err != nil {
214				if c := logger.Check(zapcore.DebugLevel, "backConn write failed"); c != nil {
215					c.Write(zap.Error(err))
216				}
217				result = streamResultError
218				return
219			}
220		}
221	
222		// Ensure the hijacked client connection, and the new connection established
223		// with the backend, are both closed in the event of a server shutdown. This
224		// is done by registering them. We also try to gracefully close connections
225		// we recognize as websockets.
226		// We need to make sure the client connection messages (i.e. to upstream)
227		// are masked, so we need to know whether the connection is considered the
228		// server or the client side of the proxy.
229		gracefulClose := func(conn io.ReadWriteCloser, isClient bool) func() error {
230			if isWebsocket(req) {
231				return func() error {
232					return writeCloseControl(conn, isClient)
233				}
234			}
235			return nil
236		}
237		// closing either connection from the cleanup of a config marks the stream
238		frontOpen := openConnection{&cleanupConn{conn, stream}, gracefulClose(conn, false)}
239		backOpen := openConnection{&cleanupConn{backConn, stream}, gracefulClose(backConn, true)}
240		if h.StreamDetached {
241			// detached streams belong to their upstream rather than to this handler
242			removeStream := detachedStreams.add(&detachedStream{
243				upstream: stream.upstream,
244				conns:    []openConnection{frontOpen, backOpen},
245			})
246			defer removeStream()
247		} else {
248			deleteFrontConn := h.registerConnection(frontOpen.conn, frontOpen.gracefulClose)
249			deleteBackConn := h.registerConnection(backOpen.conn, backOpen.gracefulClose)
250			defer deleteFrontConn()
251			defer deleteBackConn()
252		}
253	
254		// setup the timeout if requested
255		var timeoutc <-chan time.Time
256		if h.StreamTimeout > 0 {
257			timer := time.NewTimer(time.Duration(h.StreamTimeout))
258			defer timer.Stop()
259			timeoutc = timer.C
260		}
261	
262		// when a stream timeout is encountered, no error will be read from errc
263		// a buffer size of 2 will allow both the read and write goroutines to send the error and exit
264		// see: https://github.com/caddyserver/caddy/issues/7418
265		errc := make(chan error, 2)
266		wg.Add(2)
267		go spc.copyToBackend(errc)
268		go spc.copyFromBackend(errc)
269	
270		// Wait for both directions to finish. A clean EOF in one direction is a
271		// half-close of that direction only, not the end of the tunnel: the copier
272		// propagates it to the destination with CloseWrite and reports nil, so the
273		// other direction is left open and pending bytes can still drain. Anything
274		// else ends the tunnel: a copy error, a failed CloseWrite, or errCopyDone
275		// when the destination has no write half to close.
276		//
277		// net/http/httputil expresses the same wait as:
278		//
279		//	err := <-errc
280		//	if err == nil {
281		//		err = <-errc
282		//	}
283		//
284		// which cannot be used verbatim here because this handler also selects on the
285		// stream timeout, so the wait is repeated inside that select instead. Both
286		// accept the same sequences; the loop only additionally lets the timeout win
287		// at either wait.
288		//
289		// See https://github.com/caddyserver/caddy/issues/8026, and the same class
290		// fixed upstream in net/http/httputil (https://go.dev/issue/35892).
291		for range 2 {
292			select {
293			case err := <-errc:
294				if err != nil {
295					if c := logger.Check(zapcore.DebugLevel, "streaming error"); c != nil {
296						c.Write(zap.Error(err))
297					}
298					// a direction that ended cleanly on a connection without a
299					// write half to close is a normal end of the stream
300					if !errors.Is(err, errCopyDone) {
301						result = streamResultError
302					}
303					return
304				}
305			case time := <-timeoutc:
306				if c := logger.Check(zapcore.DebugLevel, "stream timed out"); c != nil {
307					c.Write(zap.Time("timeout", time))
308				}
309				result = streamResultTimeout
310				return
311			}
312		}
313	}
314	
315	// flushInterval returns the p.FlushInterval value, conditionally
316	// overriding its value for a specific request/response.
317	func (h Handler) flushInterval(req *http.Request, res *http.Response, incremental bool) time.Duration {
318		// The upstream asked for the response to be forwarded incrementally.
319		// See RFC 10036: https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc10036.html
320		if incremental || caddyhttp.IsIncremental(res.Header) {
321			return -1 // negative means immediately
322		}
323	
324		resCTHeader := res.Header.Get("Content-Type")
325		resCT, _, err := mime.ParseMediaType(resCTHeader)
326	
327		// For Server-Sent Events responses, flush immediately.
328		// The MIME type is defined in https://www.w3.org/TR/eventsource/#text-event-stream
329		if err == nil && resCT == "text/event-stream" {
330			return -1
331		}
332	
333		// We might have the case of streaming for which Content-Length might be unset.
334		if res.ContentLength == -1 {
335			return -1
336		}
337	
338		// for h2 and h2c upstream streaming data to client (issues #3556 and #3606)
339		if h.isBidirectionalStream(req, res) {
340			return -1
341		}
342	
343		return time.Duration(h.FlushInterval)
344	}
345	
346	// isBidirectionalStream returns whether we should work in bi-directional stream mode.
347	//
348	// See https://github.com/caddyserver/caddy/pull/3620 for discussion of nuances.
349	func (h Handler) isBidirectionalStream(req *http.Request, res *http.Response) bool {
350		// We have to check the encoding here; only flush headers with identity encoding.
351		// Non-identity encoding might combine with "encode" directive, and in that case,
352		// if body size larger than enc.MinLength, upper level encode handle might have
353		// Content-Encoding header to write.
354		// (see https://github.com/caddyserver/caddy/issues/3606 for use case)
355		ae := req.Header.Get("Accept-Encoding")
356	
357		return req.ProtoMajor == 2 &&
358			res.ProtoMajor == 2 &&
359			res.ContentLength == -1 &&
360			(ae == "identity" || ae == "")
361	}
362	
363	func (h Handler) copyResponse(dst http.ResponseWriter, src io.Reader, flushInterval time.Duration, logger *zap.Logger) error {
364		var w io.Writer = dst
365	
366		if flushInterval != 0 {
367			var mlwLogger *zap.Logger
368			if h.VerboseLogs {
369				mlwLogger = logger.Named("max_latency_writer")
370			} else {
371				mlwLogger = zap.NewNop()
372			}
373			mlw := &maxLatencyWriter{
