61	func (h *Handler) handleUpgradeResponse(logger *zap.Logger, wg *sync.WaitGroup, rw http.ResponseWriter, req *http.Request, res *http.Response) {
62		reqUpType := upgradeType(req.Header)
63		resUpType := upgradeType(res.Header)
64	
65		// Taken from https://github.com/golang/go/commit/5c489514bc5e61ad9b5b07bd7d8ec65d66a0512a
66		// We know reqUpType is ASCII, it's checked by the caller.
67		if !asciiIsPrint(resUpType) {
68			if c := logger.Check(zapcore.DebugLevel, "backend tried to switch to invalid protocol"); c != nil {
69				c.Write(zap.String("backend_upgrade", resUpType))
70			}
71			return
72		}
73		if !asciiEqualFold(reqUpType, resUpType) {
74			if c := logger.Check(zapcore.DebugLevel, "backend tried to switch to unexpected protocol via Upgrade header"); c != nil {
75				c.Write(
76					zap.String("backend_upgrade", resUpType),
77					zap.String("requested_upgrade", reqUpType),
78				)
79			}
80			return
81		}
82	
83		backConn, ok := res.Body.(io.ReadWriteCloser)
84		if !ok {
85			logger.Error("internal error: 101 switching protocols response with non-writable body")
86			return
87		}
88	
89		if h.StreamLogs != nil && h.StreamLogs.SkipHandshake {
90			caddyhttp.SetVar(req.Context(), caddyhttp.LogSkipVar, true)
91		}
92	
93		// write header first, response headers should not be counted in size
94		// like the rest of handler chain.
95		copyHeader(rw.Header(), res.Header)
96		normalizeWebsocketHeaders(rw.Header())
97	
98		var (
99			conn io.ReadWriteCloser
100			brw  *bufio.ReadWriter
101		)
102		// websocket over http2 or http3 if extended connect is enabled, assuming backend doesn't support this, the request will be modified to http1.1 upgrade
103		// TODO: once we can reliably detect backend support this, it can be removed for those backends
104		if body, ok := caddyhttp.GetVar(req.Context(), "extended_connect_websocket_body").(io.ReadCloser); ok {
105			req.Body = body
106			rw.Header().Del("Upgrade")
107			rw.Header().Del("Connection")
108			delete(rw.Header(), "Sec-WebSocket-Accept")
109			rw.WriteHeader(http.StatusOK)
110	
111			if c := logger.Check(zap.DebugLevel, "upgrading connection"); c != nil {
112				c.Write(zap.Int("http_version", 2))
113			}
114	
115			//nolint:bodyclose
116			flushErr := http.NewResponseController(rw).Flush()
117			if flushErr != nil {
118				if c := h.logger.Check(zap.ErrorLevel, "failed to flush http2 websocket response"); c != nil {
119					c.Write(zap.Error(flushErr))
120				}
121				return
122			}
123			conn = h2ReadWriteCloser{req.Body, rw}
124			// bufio is not needed, use minimal buffer
125			brw = bufio.NewReadWriter(bufio.NewReaderSize(conn, 1), bufio.NewWriterSize(conn, 1))
126		} else {
127			rw.WriteHeader(res.StatusCode)
128	
129			if c := logger.Check(zap.DebugLevel, "upgrading connection"); c != nil {
130				c.Write(zap.Int("http_version", req.ProtoMajor))
131			}
132	
133			var hijackErr error
134			//nolint:bodyclose
135			conn, brw, hijackErr = http.NewResponseController(rw).Hijack()
136			if errors.Is(hijackErr, http.ErrNotSupported) {
137				if c := h.logger.Check(zap.ErrorLevel, "can't switch protocols using non-Hijacker ResponseWriter"); c != nil {
138					c.Write(zap.String("type", fmt.Sprintf("%T", rw)))
139				}
140				return
141			}
142	
143			if hijackErr != nil {
144				if c := h.logger.Check(zap.ErrorLevel, "hijack failed on protocol switch"); c != nil {
145					c.Write(zap.Error(hijackErr))
146				}
147				return
148			}
149		}
150	
151		// adopted from https://github.com/golang/go/commit/8bcf2834afdf6a1f7937390903a41518715ef6f5
152		backConnCloseCh := make(chan struct{})
153		go func() {
154			// Ensure that the cancellation of a request closes the backend.
155			// See issue https://golang.org/issue/35559.
156			select {
157			case <-req.Context().Done():
158			case <-backConnCloseCh:
159			}
160			backConn.Close()
161		}()
162	
163		// From here on the stream is open and accounted for. The deferred
164		// function below is the only place where it is accounted as closed, so
165		// each stream is counted exactly once whichever way it ends.
166		start := time.Now()
167		stream := &upgradedStream{upstream: streamUpstream(req)}
168		spc := &switchProtocolCopier{
169			user:       conn,
170			backend:    backConn,
171			wg:         wg,
172			bufferSize: h.StreamBufferSize,
173		}
174		result := streamResultCompleted
175		streamStarted()
176		defer func() {
177			close(backConnCloseCh)
178			conn.Close()
179			backConn.Close()
180			// let the copiers end so that the byte counts are final
181			wg.Wait()
182	
183			duration := time.Since(start)
184			switch {
185			case stream.closedByCleanup.Load():
186				result = streamResultReload
187			case result == streamResultError && req.Context().Err() != nil:
188				result = streamResultCanceled
189			}
190			toBackend, fromBackend := spc.bytesToBackend.Load(), spc.bytesFromBackend.Load()
191			streamFinished(result, duration, toBackend, fromBackend)
192	
193			if c := logger.Check(zapcore.DebugLevel, "connection closed"); c != nil {
194				c.Write(zap.Duration("duration", duration))
195			}
196			h.logStreamClosed(req, stream, result, duration, toBackend, fromBackend)
197		}()
198	
199		if err := brw.Flush(); err != nil {
200			if c := logger.Check(zapcore.DebugLevel, "response flush"); c != nil {
201				c.Write(zap.Error(err))
202			}
203			result = streamResultError
204			return
205		}
206	
207		// There may be buffered data in the *bufio.Reader
208		// see: https://github.com/caddyserver/caddy/issues/6273
209		if buffered := brw.Reader.Buffered(); buffered > 0 {
210			data, _ := brw.Peek(buffered)
211			n, err := backConn.Write(data)
212			spc.bytesToBackend.Add(int64(n))
213			if err != nil {
214				if c := logger.Check(zapcore.DebugLevel, "backConn write failed"); c != nil {
215					c.Write(zap.Error(err))
216				}
217				result = streamResultError
218				return
219			}
220		}
221	
222		// Ensure the hijacked client connection, and the new connection established
223		// with the backend, are both closed in the event of a server shutdown. This
224		// is done by registering them. We also try to gracefully close connections
225		// we recognize as websockets.
226		// We need to make sure the client connection messages (i.e. to upstream)
227		// are masked, so we need to know whether the connection is considered the
228		// server or the client side of the proxy.
229		gracefulClose := func(conn io.ReadWriteCloser, isClient bool) func() error {
230			if isWebsocket(req) {
231				return func() error {
232					return writeCloseControl(conn, isClient)
233				}
234			}
235			return nil
236		}
237		// closing either connection from the cleanup of a config marks the stream
238		frontOpen := openConnection{&cleanupConn{conn, stream}, gracefulClose(conn, false)}
239		backOpen := openConnection{&cleanupConn{backConn, stream}, gracefulClose(backConn, true)}
240		if h.StreamDetached {
241			// detached streams belong to their upstream rather than to this handler
242			removeStream := detachedStreams.add(&detachedStream{
243				upstream: stream.upstream,
244				conns:    []openConnection{frontOpen, backOpen},
245			})
246			defer removeStream()
247		} else {
248			deleteFrontConn := h.registerConnection(frontOpen.conn, frontOpen.gracefulClose)
249			deleteBackConn := h.registerConnection(backOpen.conn, backOpen.gracefulClose)
250			defer deleteFrontConn()
251			defer deleteBackConn()
252		}
253	
254		// setup the timeout if requested
255		var timeoutc <-chan time.Time
256		if h.StreamTimeout > 0 {
257			timer := time.NewTimer(time.Duration(h.StreamTimeout))
258			defer timer.Stop()
259			timeoutc = timer.C
260		}
261	
262		// when a stream timeout is encountered, no error will be read from errc
263		// a buffer size of 2 will allow both the read and write goroutines to send the error and exit
264		// see: https://github.com/caddyserver/caddy/issues/7418
265		errc := make(chan error, 2)
266		wg.Add(2)
267		go spc.copyToBackend(errc)
268		go spc.copyFromBackend(errc)
269	
270		// Wait for both directions to finish. A clean EOF in one direction is a
271		// half-close of that direction only, not the end of the tunnel: the copier
272		// propagates it to the destination with CloseWrite and reports nil, so the
273		// other direction is left open and pending bytes can still drain. Anything
274		// else ends the tunnel: a copy error, a failed CloseWrite, or errCopyDone
275		// when the destination has no write half to close.
276		//
277		// net/http/httputil expresses the same wait as:
278		//
279		//	err := <-errc
280		//	if err == nil {
281		//		err = <-errc
282		//	}
283		//
284		// which cannot be used verbatim here because this handler also selects on the
285		// stream timeout, so the wait is repeated inside that select instead. Both
286		// accept the same sequences; the loop only additionally lets the timeout win
287		// at either wait.
288		//
289		// See https://github.com/caddyserver/caddy/issues/8026, and the same class
290		// fixed upstream in net/http/httputil (https://go.dev/issue/35892).
291		for range 2 {
292			select {
293			case err := <-errc:
294				if err != nil {
295					if c := logger.Check(zapcore.DebugLevel, "streaming error"); c != nil {
296						c.Write(zap.Error(err))
297					}
298					// a direction that ended cleanly on a connection without a
299					// write half to close is a normal end of the stream
300					if !errors.Is(err, errCopyDone) {
301						result = streamResultError
302					}
303					return
304				}
305			case time := <-timeoutc:
306				if c := logger.Check(zapcore.DebugLevel, "stream timed out"); c != nil {
307					c.Write(zap.Time("timeout", time))
308				}
309				result = streamResultTimeout
310				return
311			}
312		}
313	}

315	// flushInterval returns the p.FlushInterval value, conditionally
316	// overriding its value for a specific request/response.
317	func (h Handler) flushInterval(req *http.Request, res *http.Response, incremental bool) time.Duration {
318		// The upstream asked for the response to be forwarded incrementally.
319		// See RFC 10036: https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc10036.html
320		if incremental || caddyhttp.IsIncremental(res.Header) {
321			return -1 // negative means immediately
322		}
323	
324		resCTHeader := res.Header.Get("Content-Type")
325		resCT, _, err := mime.ParseMediaType(resCTHeader)
326	
327		// For Server-Sent Events responses, flush immediately.
328		// The MIME type is defined in https://www.w3.org/TR/eventsource/#text-event-stream
329		if err == nil && resCT == "text/event-stream" {
330			return -1
331		}
332	
333		// We might have the case of streaming for which Content-Length might be unset.
334		if res.ContentLength == -1 {
335			return -1
336		}
337	
338		// for h2 and h2c upstream streaming data to client (issues #3556 and #3606)
339		if h.isBidirectionalStream(req, res) {
340			return -1
341		}
342	
343		return time.Duration(h.FlushInterval)
344	}
345	
346	// isBidirectionalStream returns whether we should work in bi-directional stream mode.
347	//
348	// See https://github.com/caddyserver/caddy/pull/3620 for discussion of nuances.
349	func (h Handler) isBidirectionalStream(req *http.Request, res *http.Response) bool {
350		// We have to check the encoding here; only flush headers with identity encoding.
351		// Non-identity encoding might combine with "encode" directive, and in that case,
352		// if body size larger than enc.MinLength, upper level encode handle might have
353		// Content-Encoding header to write.
354		// (see https://github.com/caddyserver/caddy/issues/3606 for use case)
355		ae := req.Header.Get("Accept-Encoding")
356	
357		return req.ProtoMajor == 2 &&
358			res.ProtoMajor == 2 &&
359			res.ContentLength == -1 &&
360			(ae == "identity" || ae == "")
361	}
